title: French Bulldog Vomiting: Causes and Warning Signs
description: French Bulldog vomiting: identify the difference from regurgitation, possible causes, emergency warning signs and when to call your veterinarian.
seoTitle: French Bulldog Vomiting: Causes & When to Worry
imageAlt: Educational comparison chart: vomiting involves active abdominal effort while regurgitation is mostly passive; emergency warning signs below

faq.q: Why is my French Bulldog throwing up after eating?
faq.a: The material may be true vomiting or passive regurgitation. Airway or esophageal conditions and many digestive disorders can contribute. Repeated episodes should be assessed by a veterinarian.

faq.q: What's the difference between vomiting and regurgitation?
faq.a: Vomiting generally involves nausea, retching and active belly contractions. Regurgitation is usually passive, often with undigested food. Video of an episode can help a veterinarian.

faq.q: When is vomiting an emergency for a French Bulldog?
faq.a: Seek urgent care for an enlarged abdomen with repeated unproductive retching, collapse, blood, suspected poisoning or obstruction, or difficulty breathing.

faq.q: What can I give my French Bulldog for vomiting?
faq.a: Do not give human medications or start fasting a puppy without veterinary advice. Keep water available unless your veterinarian instructs otherwise and ask for an assessment if vomiting persists.
